title: Projection commutes with one step
statement: Let $P$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $A$, let $l$ be a natural number, choose a work-tape index $h$ of $P$, a finite data-state set $D$ with initial state $d_0$, and any visit function of the specified type. Suppose every transition of $P$ emits no output symbol. For every input word $x$ and every configuration $c$ of the decorated machine on $x$, projecting the result of one decorated-machine step from $c$ onto the schedule equals the result of one step of $P$ from the schedule projection of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is finite and has decidable equality
$P$ is a finite Turing machine over $A$
The visit function has the stated type
Every transition of $P$ emits no output symbol
$c$ is a configuration of the decorated machine on $x$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a machine over an alphabet $A$ whose transition table never emits an
output symbol, and consider its decoration by any data transducer with $l$ extra
tapes, designated head, initial data state, and visit function. For every
configuration $c$ of the decorated machine, the schedule projection of one step of
the decorated machine at $c$ equals one step of $P$ at the schedule projection of
$c$. This is an equality of entire configurations, not merely a correspondence at
macrostep boundaries.
